newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares edge up on Benelux.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares edge up on Benelux.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed slightly higher on Friday, thanks to sharp gains by floppy disk maker Benelux, brokers said.
The B share index rose 0.49 points, or 0.54 percent, to close at 90.00, but turnover shrank to HK$12.42 million from HK$29.62 million in the previous session.

Brokers said the B share advance was partly due to Benelux, which surged HK$0.45, or 18.00 percent, to HK$2.95 on volume of 8,800 on speculative buying. They said they expected the counter to fall back in the short term because of the thin trade.

There had been signs lately that overseas institutions have been patiently building positions in several large-cap issues expected to post strong results this year, said an analyst with Shenzhen-based China Southern Securities.
Southern Glass was the third most active issue, up HK$0.18 or 5.66 percent, to HK$3.36 on trade of 298,038 shares.

Dadonghai inched up HK$0.01 to HK$1.30 on the session's heaviest trade of 867,300 shares. Guangdong Power, which posted a strong performance on Thursday, fell back HK$0.01 to HK$5.41, with 542,400 shares traded.

Great Ocean, the sharpest gainer on Thursday, declined HK$0.05, or 2.35 percent, to HK$2.08. Motorcycle producer North Jianshe fell HK$0.03 to HK$2.20 as 156,900 shares changed hands on investor pessimism over its 1996 earnings, brokers said.

The A share market reversed early losses with, adding 0.79 points, or 0.21 percent, to 373.86. Turnover fell to 10.02 billion yuan from Thursday's 10.32 billion. The composite index firmed 0.78 points, or 0.23 percent, to 348.36.
Shenzhen-based property issue Baoheng was the day's star on speculative demand by institutions, brokers said. The counter soared 1.71 yuan, or 16.93 per cent, to 11.81 yuan.
Kunshan Sanshan followed suit, surging 0.76 yuan, or 12.52 percent, to 6.83 yuan, though the chemical fibre maker reported losses last year and in the first half of 1996.

Trading in A and B shares of Shenzhen Gintian Industry Co Ltd was suspended in the afternoon pending an announcement by the conglomerate and trading will resume on Monday morning, the Shenzhen bourse said in a notice.

A Gintian spokesman said there had been widespread rumours about the company lately, which had led to a steep rise in the price of its A shares and active trade and that it would make public a notice denying the rumours.
